_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-23 · SkyBound (Session 184) finished the funding model with two changes. A maximum allocation now sits beside the minimum, editable, at $400,000 — but measuring it first changed the story: it holds two colleges and moves about a third of a percent, because a college already pinned to the minimum cannot be lifted by a maximum. Then the rural allowance came out and the minimum went up to $175,000 in its place, which pays those 13 colleges $236,406 more than the allowance ever did. Ten of the 13 would not have moved a dollar without the raise, and three would have gone backwards. Separately: Sierra is down on a billing balance, and your noncredit question now has numbers under it — noncredit turns out to be 111 institutions, not four.
_status: The funding model is where you left it plus one dial fewer. Two bounds, both editable in one box: a $175,000 minimum and a $400,000 maximum. The rural allowance is gone from every screen, the CSV and the college rows; the rural flag itself stays in the data because it is a true fact about those colleges, it just no longer moves money. Three things want you rather than a session. The pair of numbers is your call and the alternative you floated — hold the minimum at $150,000 and send the freed million to noncredit — is costed and ready either way. The noncredit question has an answer now, and it is bigger than expected: 111 institutions carry noncredit, so the floor you named only fits if the roster is scoped, and a 500-FTES cut-off fits inside the existing million. And Sierra is returning errors on an empty Anthropic balance, which nothing alerts on. Nothing else is blocked; the model is correct at any setting of the dials.

items.text: Pick the floor and ceiling pair. Live right now: a $175,000 minimum and a $400,000 maximum, both editable side by side in the Funding pools box. What that pair actually does: 69 of the 115 colleges land on the minimum — the middle college in the state is now funded by the minimum rather than by its size — and the maximum holds only two colleges and moves $82,815, about a third of one percent. So the minimum is doing nearly all the work and the maximum is close to decoration at this level. The cost is real and worth seeing before you settle: a floor is paid for by the colleges above it, so a mid-sized college now earns $4,419 per CPL FTES against the $5,650 statewide rate — 78 cents on the dollar. The alternative you floated is still open and still costed: hold the minimum at $150,000 and send the freed $1,000,000 to noncredit instead. Both are the same change with two different dial settings.

Decide how wide the noncredit lane should be. You asked what a $25,000 floor and $100,000 ceiling would look like for our other noncredit institutions, and the first number reframes the question: noncredit is not four institutions, it is 111. One hundred and eight of the 115 credit colleges already carry noncredit FTES, alongside the three standalone continuing-education institutions. At that width the numbers you named do not fit — 111 floors of $25,000 is $2,775,000, nearly three times the $1,000,000 carve-out, and still short even if the retired rural million is added on top. At exactly that figure everyone sits on the floor and the FTES basis does nothing at all. The lever is the roster, not the bounds: institutions with 500 or more noncredit FTES are 33 of them and carry 87 percent of the lane, and they fit inside the existing $1,000,000 — 27 at the $25,000 floor, the largest at $89,586, the ceiling never binding. Two cautions. Mt. SAC's noncredit FTES is currently counted twice in our data, which is harmless today and wrong the day noncredit money follows that number. And 'only what came from the noncredit landing pages' is a rule the data feed cannot tell apart yet — sizing the pool is the easy half.

Read 'How this funding model works' end to end in a browser before you send it to anyone. It is the audience-facing walk-through for the Chancellor's Office and possibly Finance, and the link now sits at the top right of the Implementation Funding title row. It has been rebuilt twice since you last saw it: the maximum is in it, the rural allowance is out of it, and the minimum is $175,000 — so the opening figures, the count of colleges at the minimum (69 now, was 45) and the worked example have all changed. The worked example is Long Beach, because the two largest colleges are now pinned to a round number their own share does not explain. No session can look at it; the sandbox cannot reach the site. One footnote: if you are still commenting on an older copy of this page, those comments do not reach the version the tab links to — comment on the linked one, and tell us when you have, because nothing pings us automatically.

Decide whether Sierra should know which page she is on. You asked whether My College should have its own Sierra setup. Our recommendation is no separate Sierra — that would mean every future fix has to be made in several places and one will get missed — but yes to telling her which surface she is on, so a My College instruction stops being read on the public page. About a day's work. One caveat: it cannot make her behave in a way that contradicts her built-in rules; that would be a bigger change.

MAP needs to give us two college IDs. You ruled that Calbright and LAUNCH each have two entities — one credit, one noncredit. The noncredit halves already have IDs; the credit halves ("Calbright College Credit" and "Launch Apprenticeship Non-Credit") have none anywhere we can see, and MAP is the only system allowed to assign one. We deliberately did NOT make one up, because a fake ID would look exactly like a real one to every other system. They show as "awaiting MAP ID" on the College Identity tab. Once MAP supplies them, they fold in with no code change.

Take a look at the new College Identity tab. It lists every college and agency we track, its MAP ID, its district, its state MIS code, and every different spelling of its name we have ever seen. Its real job is showing what is MISSING — right now it flags 13 names that appear in a live table and match nothing. Two of those turned out to be a genuine problem: Cypress College and San Jose City College had a stray space at the end of their name in the contacts table, so both looked like they had no CPL contact when they each have a real one. Already fixed.
Twelve credentials are marked statewide in the adoption file but are missing from Sierra's catalog entirely, so she cannot find them at all. Carried from an earlier session and still open.

Fix smoke test mode 7 so it stops failing on correct answers. It reads Sierra's reply and searches the sentences for particular college names, so she can give a good answer and still fail. It went red again today on a change that could not possibly have affected it. Do NOT fix it by deleting the check — the test's own comment says that part matters most to someone looking for somewhere local to go. Check instead that a nearby college reached her at all, and leave the wording to mode 8, which already tests the same thing properly.

Please open the three public pages on your phone — the Fact Sheet, Sierra, and the Veteran Sprint map. This is the last thing no session can check: we are blocked from reaching the live site, so all of it is verified in a test browser only. On the Fact Sheet, scroll to Statewide CPL credit recommendations — each program area should sit on its own line with four labelled figures beneath it (Exhibits, Credit recs, Adoptions, Could adopt); before the fix the name printed on top of the first number and Could adopt was cut off entirely. On the Veteran map, the side panel with the college details and the two directories was being hidden completely on any phone — it should now sit below the map. On Sierra, the faint grey notes under the answer box should be readable. If anything looks cramped or odd, tell me and I will tune it.

Give Calbright Credit and Launch Non-Credit a placeholder row so they stop disappearing. They are missing from the identity table entirely, which means they silently fall out of four other tables rather than showing up as a known gap. A row with no ID and a stated reason is safe; inventing an ID is not.

One of MAP's test colleges is sitting in Sierra's data. "Las PosTest College" is in the catalog Sierra reads, and the filter that hides sandbox rows elsewhere cannot reach that table. It is empty, so the worst case is Sierra mentioning a college that does not exist — but it should not be reachable at all.

Join our tables on MAP's college ID instead of the college name. Sam asked whether we are making the best use of location IDs rather than text — measured, and he is right: 13 tables carry MAP's ID, 18 do not, and the ones that do not are all the tables we build ourselves. That is why a stray space in a college name could hide a real CPL coordinator. Four colleges' contacts are currently found only through the variant list we added last week.

Have a look at the tabs now that text runs the full width. You said the short text columns look awkward against the full-width tables, so every paragraph across 17 files now runs to the same right edge as the tables beside it. Nobody has seen it rendered. If it reads too wide, two columns is the alternative and it is a single switch, not a rebuild.

Sierra is down right now, and it is billing, not code. Every question that needs the model comes back with 'your credit balance is too low' — a student asking her something today gets an error. Everything that does not need the model still answers, so the service itself is healthy. Two things to do: top up the Anthropic balance, and decide how we find out next time. Nobody was told this time; a session happened to notice. The cheap option is an alert when she starts returning errors; the expensive one is running her test suite every hour, which costs money every run and is what drained the balance in the first place. We have not built either, on purpose, because it is your call.
